title: Vegetative propagation of mosses under controlled conditions: A reproducible, low-cost method for sustainable moss cultivation☆☆☆
author: Strazdina, Abele, et al.
materials: Materials: gloves, scissors, hemp mats, reverse osmosis water.

steps.title: Collect mosses in the field
steps.instruction: Wear gloves, obtain a collection permit, and use 15 L plastic trays as transport containers. Manually collect moss clumps from forest habitats, gently brush away pine needles, branches, and cones, detach the clumps, and place them into the trays. Fill gaps left on the forest floor with adjacent mosses and sample from multiple sites to minimise ecological disturbance.

steps.title: Trim and clean harvested moss
steps.instruction: Using scissors (while wearing gloves), divide each sample into the green, photosynthetically active portion and the lower brown, decayed portion; discard the decayed material. Remove any residual organic debris such as pine needles, bark fragments, or branches so that only clean, viable moss remains.

steps.title: Store or immediately moisten moss
steps.instruction: If processing cannot be done immediately, store the trimmed moss in 15 L plastic trays at room temperature for no longer than five days to avoid desiccation. When ready to use, moisten the moss by gently squeezing it several times with reverse‑osmosis (RO) water until the fragments are fully saturated (sponge‑like).

steps.title: Prepare pre‑wet hemp substrate
steps.instruction: Lay out non‑woven hemp fiber mats (60 × 60 × 0.4 cm) and pre‑wet them with RO water. Hemp fiber provides high water‑retention but can decompose and foster mould under constant moisture, so note this risk.

steps.title: Distribute moss onto hemp mats
steps.instruction: Manually spread the saturated moss fragments over each pre‑wet hemp mat until the growing material is barely visible through the layer. Aim for near‑complete coverage (90–100 % of the mat surface); coverage of 50–90 % leads to drying, yellowing, and loss of vigor.

steps.title: Transfer mats to climate facility
steps.instruction: Place the prepared hemp mats (each 0.36 m²) directly on a plastic‑covered floor inside the climate‑controlled room to prevent contact with the underlying surface and reduce soil‑derived contamination. A total of 200 such tiles may be used, with species composition varying per tile as desired.

steps.title: Configure growing room environment
steps.instruction: Use a 124 m² growing room whose floor is covered with waterproof plastic. Add a 3 mm thick reflective thermal‑insulation foil (laminated on one side) and a waterproof plastic film for additional floor protection. Install LED projectors (200 W, 17 600 lm, bright white 6500 K) for illumination, household fans for ventilation, and a 15 L electric water pulverizer for fogging irrigation.

steps.title: Run four‑month cultivation cycle
steps.instruction: Cultivate the mosses for four months (June–September 2025) under the configured conditions. Adjust watering cycles, ventilation intensity, and fertilisation frequency iteratively until stable establishment is observed. Expect moss height of 1–2 cm and surface coverage >80 % by the end of the period. No biomass measurements or destructive sampling are required.

steps.title: Control mould with hydrogen peroxide
steps.instruction: Spray the mosses with hydrogen‑peroxide solution twice per week, maintaining a three‑day interval between applications. Test concentrations sequentially: 0.25 %, 0.5 %, 0.75 %, 1.0 %, 1.25 %, 1.5 %, 1.75 %, and 2.0 %. Concentrations ≥1.5 % cause visible chlorosis; concentrations >1.25 % intensify discoloration. Therefore, do not exceed 1.25 % (the highest recommended concentration).
